title: Debug the Backup Script
description: Repair /usr/local/bin/backup.sh: wrong shebang, no gzip, wrong output path and no proper exit status.
scenario: Last night's backup did not produce a usable archive. The previous admin's script at /usr/local/bin/backup.sh is a mess: the shebang is mangled, it creates a plain .tar instead of the documented .tar.gz, and it does not exit with a meaningful status. The web app it should back up lives in /var/www/app. Fix the script so a run produces /tmp/backups/app-backup.tar.gz containing the app files.
symptoms: After running, /tmp/backups contains app-backup.tar instead of app-backup.tar.gz
The script's first line is the nonsense '#bash/bin' so direct execution picks the wrong interpreter
The final echo prints a path built from a different variable than the tar command used
The script never sets an explicit exit status for the scheduler to check
mission: Repair backup.sh so that: `bash -n` passes, it creates /tmp/backups/app-backup.tar.gz (gzipped tar) from /var/www/app, prints that path, and exits 0 on success.

hints.title: Syntax check first
hints.content: `bash -n script` parses the script without executing it — the fastest way to catch mangled lines.

hints.title: The shebang
hints.content: It must read exactly `#!/bin/bash`. Anything else (like #bash/bin) is just a comment to sh and the script runs under the wrong shell.

hints.title: Compress while archiving
hints.content: `tar czf <file>.tar.gz <dir>` compresses with gzip in one step — the 'z' flag is what the current script is missing.

hints.title: Exit status
hints.content: Finish with `exit 0` so the cron/scheduler sees success; after a failed tar you would `exit 1`.

acceptance_criteria.description: backup.sh passes a bash syntax check (bash -n)
the archive contains the app's index.html
